around.headline: Yellow Line back to normal after Monday's fatal incident; platform screen door demand revives
around.summary: A passenger died after jumping in front of a train at Huskur Road station on Monday evening, disrupting Yellow Line services for over two hours; the tragedy has renewed calls for platform screen doors on the line. Services are back to normal for this morning's commute.

around.headline: Two airport runways to allow parallel departures from September; four Pink Line stations get two-wheeler parking
around.summary: Kempegowda International Airport will enable parallel departures on two runways from September, and four elevated Pink Line metro stations are getting two-wheeler parking bays. Both should ease peak-time congestion for flyers and metro commuters once live.

around.headline: Bengaluru police recover over 1,100 missing mobile phones
around.summary: City police traced and returned more than 1,100 lost or stolen mobile phones to their owners. If your phone is ever stolen, block it immediately via the CEIR portal (ceir.gov.in) with your IMEI number — it's what makes recoveries like this possible.

around.headline: BJP alleges Rs 800 crore KPSC recruitment scam, says 'jobs sold for money'
around.summary: Opposition leader R Ashoka has alleged a Rs 800 crore scam in Karnataka Public Service Commission recruitments. Whatever the political fallout, treat it as a reminder: genuine government recruitment never requires paying anyone privately for a result.

around.headline: Greater Bengaluru Authority notifies new building approval fee structure
around.summary: The GBA has notified a revised fee structure for building plan approvals. Anyone planning construction or renovation should check the new rates before applying rather than budgeting off old BBMP figures.

around.headline: Oil prices plunge 5% after US and Iran halt attacks
around.summary: Crude oil prices dropped around 5% after the US and Iran signalled a halt to attacks amid West Asia tensions. If the trend holds, it could feed through to lower pump prices in the coming weeks.

street_smart.title: You bought a smartwatch online. It stops working within a week, and the seller says 'no returns after unboxing' and stops replying. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen topic (consumer court basics) — no single incident in today's feeds fit this scenario cleanly, and recent street-smart topics (job scams, phone theft, card skimming) were used within the last 3 weeks.
street_smart.situation: The product is clearly defective, well within the return window most platforms advertise, but the seller is citing a blanket 'no returns' policy and has gone silent on chat.

choices.text: File a free complaint on the National Consumer Helpline (call 1915, or use consumerhelpline.gov.in / the UMANG app), citing that the product is defective.
choices.feedback: Correct. Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, a seller's 'no returns' clause does not override your right to a refund or replacement for a defective product — the helpline mediates with the seller directly and it costs nothing.

choices.text: Accept the seller's 'no returns after unboxing' policy and write off the loss.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Sellers often bluff a blanket store policy against buyers who don't know it doesn't apply to defective goods — the mechanism is that 'no returns' clauses are void for genuine product defects under consumer law, and most buyers give up simply because they assume the policy is final.

choices.text: Post a public complaint or negative review threatening to make it go viral until the seller responds.
choices.feedback: This sometimes gets a seller's attention, but there's no guaranteed remedy, it's slower and less predictable than a formal complaint, and exaggerated claims in a public post can expose you to a defamation counter-claim.

choices.text: Dispute the charge directly with your bank or card issuer for a refund.
choices.feedback: A card chargeback can work, but only within a strict time window and only for card payments — it doesn't apply if you paid by UPI, and it doesn't create any record that helps if the seller is scamming other buyers too.

takeaways: Call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 (free) or use consumerhelpline.gov.in — it handles seller disputes without a lawyer.
For formal cases, e-daakhil.nic.in lets you file a consumer court complaint online, no lawyer required, for claims up to ₹50 lakh.
Keep screenshots of the product listing, any claims made, and your full chat with the seller — that's your evidence if it escalates.

quiz.q: What disrupted Namma Metro's Yellow Line for over two hours on Monday?
options: A passenger's death at Huskur Road station
quiz.why: The incident has revived long-standing demands for platform screen doors on the Yellow Line, a safety feature already common on some other metro systems.

quiz.q: What did the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) notify this week, according to Monday's reports?
options: A revised building plan approval fee structure
quiz.why: The GBA is the new civic governance layer for greater Bengaluru, replacing the erstwhile BBMP's sole charge over such municipal functions.

quiz.q: Crude oil prices dropped around 5% on Monday after which development?
options: The US and Iran signalled a halt to attacks
quiz.why: India imports over 80% of its crude oil, so sustained drops in global prices can eventually flow through to pump prices at home.

quiz.q: Bengaluru's drinking water mainly comes from which river, pumped over 100 km uphill into the city?
quiz.why: Lifting Cauvery water up roughly 300 metres in elevation to reach Bengaluru is one of the largest water-pumping operations in the world, and one reason it's an expensive resource for the city.

quiz.q: Which vitamin does your skin produce from UV exposure — even on an overcast, rainy day like today?
quiz.why: Clouds block visible light more than UV rays, which is why sunburn (and vitamin D synthesis) can still happen on a cloudy monsoon day.
